The eternal rumor: Will Microsoft dump Windows Mobile and go for Android?
Site has a crappy layout I know, but interesting none the less.

I actually really want windows phone to succeed and give us a third real competitor in the phone market. I don't think they will be giving up any time soon. That site shows an extremely slight upward trend in windows phone use, and not too long ago I heard a non-technical person express knowledge in the existence of Windows Phone and that was in fact different from "Apple and Samsung" so, that's something.

All it takes is one killer device and a little more work getting app developers to add windows phone to their workflow. But I'm not a dev so I don't know how easy of a change that actually is to make.

I know they have almost been giving away windows phones lately. People are still using them that's for sure. Personally I don't care for them and I have used one. Harder to navigate and app availability was very limited. Only slightly better than my experience with the old Windows Mobile. But, I am what people call an Android fanatic anyway.
While I didn't totally dislike it, I definitely didn't contemplate a switch . Although if it survives and matures for a couple more years, who knows?

I think getting developers to create quality apps for Windows Phone is the biggest and most likely insurmountable hurdle. If you've ever looked at the Windows App Store it really is just a handful of the ultra popular commercial apps, a very few good indie apps, and a ton of just plain crappy apps. I doubt that it is financially viable to develop or port to Windows. But back on topic, I don't see MS ever giving up on it and moving to Android.
If Microsoft doesn't support desktop applications for WinMo. I would get WinMo if it could run Windows programs.
If so, why spend so much effort on Windows Phone? It doesn't make sense, these rumors.

Not really sure. Some companies as big as Microsoft will continue to do things even at a loss.Think Phillips CDI https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philips_CD-i Or the Nokia Gage https://en.m.wikipedia.org/wiki/N-Gage They think their luck will change any minute. But in the tech world the old saying is adapt or die.

I think it's possible that they could create some android devices - but I'm sure they are still going to develop more resources for Windows Phone. It's the underdog, but I think they want to maintain their OS - just because it's worth investing in for the future. Nothing lasts forever, and android might not be as desirable to a consumer 3-5 years from now. Someone will need to be there with a compelling product (if that product would be something developed by Microsoft, I'm not sure - but options are good).
With the amount of effort they're putting into unifying Windows 10 and Windows 10 Mobile, it's probably kind of ridiculous to think that Microsoft would abandon W10M unless both W10 and W10M fail.

Betteridge's law of headlines: any headline that ends in a question mark can be answered with the word "no."

And I agree with those in here who say that it's unlikely in the near term considering how much effort Microsoft have put into Windows Mobile.
